author: Liam O'Connor
title: All Blacks vs France: Robertson's Shock Team Picks | First Test
text:
Robertson Unveils Bold All Blacks Squad with Debutants and Positional Shifts for France Test The All Blacks are set to kick off their three-Test series against France with a squad featuring several surprising selections, signaling a new era under head coach Scott Robertson. The team, announced today, sees lock Tupou Vaa’i unexpectedly named at blindside flanker and Fabian Holland poised for his highly anticipated debut at lock.
The selection reflects a response to recent player workloads and injuries, with key players unavailable for Saturday night’s match in Dunedin. Tighthead prop Tyrel Lomax is sidelined with a calf injury, and Blues lock Patrick Tuipulotu remains absent from the squad.
Christian Lio-Willie, recently crowned a Super Rugby Pacific champion with the Crusaders, will also make his Test debut at No. 8. Robertson explained that injuries and the need to manage player fatigue heavily influenced his decisions.
Vaa’i’s move to flanker, despite having played the position in a previous Test during the 2023 World Cup, is a particularly intriguing choice, with Samipeni Finau relegated to the bench. Elsewhere in the forward pack, Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, and Fletcher Newell will form the starting front row, supported by Samisoni Taukei’aho and Pasilio Tosi as reserves. Vice-captain Ardie Savea will anchor the No. 7 jersey.
The backline sees a familiar face in Beauden Barrett starting at first-five, with Damian McKenzie providing cover from the bench. Cam Roigard has earned the starting halfback position over Cortez Ratima, while Jordie Barrett returns to second-five after a sabbatical in Ireland. Rieko Ioane and Sevu Reece will flank Will Jordan on the wings, with Jordan retaining his place at fullback.
Notably, two additional players – Ollie Norris and loose forward Du’Plessis Kirifi – are in line to make their Test debuts from the bench. Robertson emphasized the hard work and dedication of these uncapped players, stating, “This is a huge moment for these men and their families, we are all thrilled for them. For Fabian and Christian, it will be special to debut in front of a Dunedin home crowd.” He added, “Ollie and Du’Plessis have both shown their class in Super Rugby this year and we know they are ready.”
The story of Fabian Holland is particularly compelling. Born in the Netherlands, the 2.04m lock made the remarkable decision at age 14 to relocate to New Zealand to pursue his rugby aspirations. Robertson described Holland’s journey as “movie sort of stuff,” highlighting his single-minded determination to represent the All Blacks. “He’s pretty excited… from Zeeland to New Zealand – he’s come a long way,” Robertson said. “His [first] opportunity is down here under the roof.”
Robertson also acknowledged the challenge posed by the French team, stating, “Facing France is always special – they bring intensity, flair, and physicality.” He expressed confidence in the team’s preparation, adding, “As a group we have had a fantastic 10 days together preparing for the three-Test series ahead of us. We are ready for the challenge and what better place to kick it off than under the roof in Dunedin in front of a packed home crowd.”
The Test match, already sold out, promises to be a thrilling encounter as the All Blacks begin their campaign against an under-strength French squad.
